No 'GO_BACK'/'REPLACE not handled' navigator warnings this iteration — the structural change (impostazioni no longer a modal) did silence the warnings, but the primary logout expectation is still broken: after login → open-settings → logout-button → re-login, the app lands on /impostazioni (URL literally reads .../impostazioni and impostazioni-screen is visible; search-input is NOT visible). action_items: impostazioni.tsx:70 — the router.back()→setTimeout(signOut,150) approach still fails on the web preview. Suggested fixes (try in order): (1) Replace `router.back()` with `router.replace('/cerca')` (now safe because impostazioni is no longer a modal after _layout.tsx cleanup — REPLACE will not be dropped) and then setTimeout signOut for a small delay (or drop the timeout entirely). (2) Move the navigation-reset into the auth store: on successful `signIn(...)` always call `router.replace('/cerca')` (or `/`) so re-login ALWAYS lands on Cerca regardless of the last URL — this makes logout robust to any pre-signOut route. (3) Await a microtask before signOut: `router.back(); await new Promise(r=>requestAnimationFrame(()=>r(null))); signOut();` — but option (2) is the safest structural fix. Verify: login 1234 → open-settings → logout-button → login-screen → login 1234 → search-input MUST be visible AND URL should not be /impostazioni; no navigator warnings.

rca_of_issue: Impostazioni is now a normal Stack push (modal presentation removed in _layout.tsx, good). Logout onPress does: router.back(); setTimeout(signOut, 150). On web, router.back() ultimately delegates to history.back(); the URL/route update is async and NOT guaranteed to commit within 150ms before signOut() flips AuthGate to render <LoginScreen/> and unmount <Stack/>. When the user re-logs in, AuthGate re-mounts <Stack/> and Expo Router restores the current URL — which is still /impostazioni because back() never got a chance to commit — so the user sees Impostazioni instead of Cerca. Recommended fix: perform the target-route navigation in the auth store on successful signIn (`router.replace('/cerca')` inside `signIn`) so re-login is always deterministic, independent of whatever route was left in the URL by logout. Alternatively, in impostazioni.tsx logout, use `router.replace('/cerca')` (now safe since impostazioni is not a modal) instead of router.back()+timeout.
